title: Worst-path profiling: quantization tradeoffs under adversarial prompt shapes
content:
Purpose / context:
This note captures an experiment suite and early findings for 'worst-path' behavior when combining quantized model variants (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) with kernel choices and adversarial prompt shapes. The aim is to understand: 
- Where quant+kernel combos break latency SLOs (tail P95/P99) even when mean throughput looks fine.
- Which prompt shapes, batch shapes, and KV-cache patterns cause sudden quality regressions (hallucination or token deletion) at specific quant levels.
- How fallback policies should be tuned (when to switch to a higher-precision kernel/model) to minimize both cost and user-visible errors.

High-level hypothesis:
1) Many latency/cost regressions are triggered by rare long-prefix prompts or highly-branching generation patterns that disable batching and cause kernel fallback thrashing.
2) AWQ-style ultra-low-bit quantization shows acceptable average perplexity but has brittle failure modes on arithmetic-heavy tokens (numbers, code) which are amplified by some kernels that fuse attention differently.
3) GPTQ variants have smoother quality curves across sequence length but still cause memory-pressure-driven kernel re-selection that increases tail latency.

Experiment matrix (summary):
- Models: open-7B-base (baseline FP16), open-7B-int8, open-7B-awq4, open-7B-gptq-qdq
- Kernels: kernel-A (fused-attn), kernel-B (split-attn+kv-opt), kernel-C (memory-conservative), kernel-D (vectorized-matmul)
- Inputs: short-chat (len 32), long-primer (len 800 prefix), numeric-heavy (lots of digits & tables), code-generate (multi-line prompt), branching-sampling (top-p=0.95 with sampling)
- Batch shapes: single request, batch of heterogeneous shapes, continuous prefix-streaming (simulate multi-turn)
- Metrics captured: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, CUDA mem high watermark, KV cache misses, throughput variance, token-level edit-distance to FP16 baseline, LM loss delta, and a small quality rubric (pass/fail on numeric accuracy + code compile check).

Test harness notes (how we ran it):
- Running under local perf rig (A100-80GB, driver 535, CUDA 12.2), microservices pinned to 8k context, warmup=2 sequences, 25 runs per cell.
- Tooling: perf traces collected with NVTX + proprietary runtime trace; python harness logs to csv and artifacts to /artifacts/quant-worstpath/jun2026/ . See linked PR for harness changes.
- Important: we disabled autoscaler during runs to keep machine allocation stable and forced the runtime to choose kernels deterministically via env override.

Representative results (early, aggregated):
1) Long-primer, single-request:
   - FP16 baseline: P95=230ms, P99=420ms, tokens/sec=620
   - INT8 (kernel-A): P95=260ms (+13%), P99=980ms (+134%) — observed intermittent 1.1s stalls where internal kernel selected a slower fallback when KV cache grew beyond threshold. Quality delta: negligible.
   - AWQ4 (kernel-A): P95=340ms, P99=1.9s — token-level errors on numeric tables in 12% of runs (digits scrambled), LM loss delta +0.8.
   - GPTQ-QDQ (kernel-C): P95=250ms, P99=520ms — quality close to FP16, occasional memory-high watermark spikes causing kernel-C->kernel-D recompile path adding 300–600ms.

2) Branching-sampling (top-p sampling, heterogeneous batch 16):
   - Notable effect: sampling widens variance; kernels that favor vectorized matmuls (kernel-D) had much better throughput but higher single-request jitter when sample trajectories triggered longer generations. AWQ variants produced longer average sequences (looping tokens) in 7% of runs causing queueing delay.

3) Numeric-heavy prompts (short but dense with numbers):
   - AWQ often produced digit transposition errors; INT8 held up for majority but produced occasional dropout of trailing digits if combined with kernel-B due to an unlikely alignment bug in the attention accumulation routine.

Detailed observations and causal hypotheses:
- KV-cache growth + dynamic kernel selection: When KV cache grows above a threshold (~12k tokens stored), the runtime switches to a memory-conservative kernel. For some quant nets (AWQ), that kernel has different accumulation ordering and loses numerical stability in specific sub-blocks, causing both quality regressions and sporadic extra latency for in-place conversion steps.
- Batch heterogeneity increases kernel selection churn: Mixed sizes force runtime to pick a kernel that can handle worst-shape. Kernel-A is fastest for uniform batches but performs poorly on mixed shapes and triggers fallback paths more frequently with AWQ quantization metadata set.
- Sampling and output length feedback: Low-bit quantization appears to subtly increase propensity to generate repetition under sampling, which in turn increases per-request generation time and amplifies tail latency.
- Memory-pressure-induced JIT/compilation: GPU memory spikes cause kernel re-allocations and possibly JIT recompiles. These events align with P99 spikes in the traces. GPTQ variants caused more memory churn (extra buffers for dequant staging) than INT8.

Immediate actionable items (runtime engineering):
1) Add a lightweight kernel-maturity signal: if a quant+kernel combo has hit a quality-failure signature N times in x window, steer new requests to fallback model variant automatically.
2) Tune KV cache thresholds per quant variant and kernel: AWQ gets a lower KV-cache threshold and should trigger early fallback to non-memory conservative kernel to avoid numeric instability.
3) Sampling-aware admission control: when top-p sampling requests exceed a threshold, isolate them into separate worker pools to avoid contaminating latency for deterministic workloads.
4) Add deterministic test vectors (numeric tables + code snippet suite) into CI and run them for every quant+kernal integration change.
5) Instrument per-request kernel-change events in traces and expose a dashboard for rapid triage.

Open questions for follow-up experiments:
- Is the digit-transposition reproducible with a minimal unit test (we have a candidate failing prompt, need to reduce it)?
- Can we reproduce KV-cache induced instability on smaller GPUs (T4) to understand hardware interaction?
- Is there a micro-architectural reason kernel-A's accumulation ordering loses fidelity with AWQ? (instrument FP32 accumulation traces locally)
- How much of AWQ failures are due to quantization tables vs. per-layer scale clipping? Run layerwise ablation.

Rough action timeline (2–6 weeks):
- Week 0–1: Create minimal failing tests and add to CI; add kernel-change tranche metrics to runtime traces (owner: Mateo).
- Week 1–3: Run ablation on layerwise quant scales for AWQ + kernel-A; run small-GPU cross-checks (owner: Lin).
- Week 2–4: Implement KV-cache per-quant thresholds + sampling worker pool prototype (owner: Riya).
- Week 3–6: Roll canary with new steering policies on Dedicated cluster with traffic mirror. If P99 drops <30% and quality regressions resolved, expand rollout.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally a working log. I included raw per-cell numbers above — full CSVs and traces are archived in the linked artifacts.
- The focus here is worst-path and tail-latency; we did not optimize for mean token cost. That will be a separate sweep once steering/fallback logic stabilizes.
- Please flag any additional failure modes your team sees in the field (SRE traces, customer reports).

Appendix (short reproducer snippets and quick commands):
- Minimal reproducer (python harness):
  python3 perf_harness.py --model open-7B-awq4 --kernel kernel-A --prompt-file tests/repro/numeric_transpose.txt --max-tokens 400 --sampling 0.95 --runs 25

- Trace visualizations: nvprof + runtime-nvtx.json -> scripts/plot-tail.py --input artifacts/quant-worstpath/jun2026/run-*/trace.json

- CI test to add: tests/quant-stability/numeric-table-transpose.test (should compile to a deterministic pass/fail).

Signed-off-by: Avery
